title: Normalized derived global sections after pro-etale direct image
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $f:T\to Y$ and $g:Y\to W$ be morphisms of $k$-schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Use the ordinary constant-$A$ module categories on small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], their bounded-below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], and their direct images and exact inverse images [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Derived global sections mean the right derived evaluation at the final object; use the finite derived direct image of [def-weil-derived-direct-image].

There is a canonical natural isomorphism of functors on $D^+(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$
$$\ell_f:R\Gamma(Y,Rf_*(-))\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(T,-).$$
On a bounded-below K-injective representative $J$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex] of $L$ it is induced by the identity of section complexes $\Gamma(Y,f_*J)=\Gamma(T,J)$. This is natural for all derived morphisms, not only chain maps between specified complexes, and compatible with shifts. For the canonical direct-image composition comparison $c_{g,f}:R(gf)_*\cong Rg_*Rf_*$ [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition], one has
$$\ell_{gf,L}=\ell_{f,L}\circ\ell_{g,Rf_*L}\circ R\Gamma(W,c_{g,f,L}).$$
The comparison for an identity is the identity. If $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], the composite
$$R\Gamma(T,L)\xrightarrow{R\Gamma(T,\eta_j)}R\Gamma(T,Rj_*j^*L)\xrightarrow{\ell_{j,j^*L}}R\Gamma(U,j^*L)$$
is the canonical restriction map, where $\eta_j$ is the open adjunction unit. In particular these comparisons identify derived global sections of a pushed-forward support-localization triangle with derived global sections of the original triangle, with the same third arrow and its shift comparison.

proof.text: Work on compatible small site models from [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The coefficient sheaf in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] is identified with the ordinary constant ring sheaf, preserving constants and the structural coefficient map, by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. All functors below are in these ordinary module categories. Choose a complex representing $L$. If its cohomology vanishes below $a$, replace it by its good truncation with degree $a$ term $K^a/\operatorname{im}(d^{a-1})$, original terms above $a$ and zero terms below $a$. The quotient map is a quasi-isomorphism: in degree $a$ its kernel modulo boundaries is $H^a(K)$, above $a$ the cohomology is unchanged, and below $a$ both cohomologies vanish. Thus [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution] supplies a bounded-below K-injective resolution $K\to J$. The same construction applies to the source of every derived morphism under consideration.

source.place: Tag 05RU, definition-unbounded-derived-category; bounded-below resolution input as stated in lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution

proof.text: The module adjunction $f^*\dashv f_*$ and exactness of $f^*$ are those of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] with $u=f_*$ and $v=f^*$: $f_*J$ is K-injective on $Y$. It is still bounded below, since an additive termwise functor sends zero terms to zero. The same applies to $g_*f_*J$ and $(gf)_*J$. Thus these particular representatives can be used without another resolution when computing any of the iterated direct images in the statement; these are exactly the finite functors in [def-weil-derived-direct-image].

By [pur7710-def-derived-sections], $R\Gamma(T,L)$ is computed by $\Gamma(T,J)$, while $R\Gamma(Y,Rf_*L)$ is computed by $\Gamma(Y,f_*J)$ using Step 2. By the sectionwise definition [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image], in degree $r$ the latter is $J^r(Y\times_YT)=J^r(T)$, using the canonical terminal-object isomorphism. This identification has the same $A$-action, restrictions, and differential on both sides. Define $\ell_{f,L}$ by the resulting identity of section complexes and the canonical resolution identifications of [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation]. It is an isomorphism, since the displayed chain map is an isomorphism in every degree.

proof.text: For any derived morphism $h:L\to L'$, choose K-injective models $J,J'$. The bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents $h$ by a unique homotopy class $b:J\to J'$. The formula of [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation] computes $Rf_*(h)$ by $f_*b$ and computes the two global-sections maps by $\Gamma(Y,f_*b)$ and $\Gamma(T,b)$. These chain maps are equal under Step 3, so the naturality square for $\ell_f$ commutes for every derived $h$. Any homotopy is carried to the same section homotopy by additive termwise evaluation. Changing $J$ or $J'$ uses precisely the transition maps of the same cited computation lemma, so the construction is independent of the resolutions. This proves canonical naturality, including maps originally given as roofs.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective, and Tag 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined; resolution-transition calculation

proof.text: The derived functors carry the shift comparisons and triangulated structures of [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. A shift of $J$ is again K-injective: maps from an acyclic $M$ into $J[n]$ correspond to maps from the acyclic $M[-n]$ into $J$, and the latter are null-homotopic. Use $J[n]$ to compute both sides of $\ell_f$ at $L[n]$. Degreewise evaluation gives $\Gamma(Y,f_*(J[n]))=\Gamma(T,J[n])=\Gamma(T,J)[n]$; all shifted differentials carry the identical factor $(-1)^n$. Thus $\ell_{f,L[n]}$ agrees with $\ell_{f,L}[n]$ through the canonical shift comparisons. Independence of resolutions in Step 4 identifies this computation with the specified derived shift comparisons.

source.place: Tag 05SU, lemma-derived-shift; Tag 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined; triangulated derived-functor input

proof.text:
Use the canonical composition comparison of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition]. Its finite ordinary module comparison is the ringed-topos comparison, whose representative is specified by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]: for a resolution $v:f_*J\to H$ it is represented by $g_*v$. Here $f_*J$ is already K-injective, so take $H=f_*J$ and $v=1$. Hence on this model $c_{g,f,L}$ is the canonical identification $(gf)_*J=g_*f_*J$. Evaluating at the final object of $W$, the right side of the asserted equation is the chain of identifications
$$\Gamma(W,(gf)_*J)=\Gamma(W,g_*f_*J)=\Gamma(Y,f_*J)=\Gamma(T,J).$$
Their composite is the direct final-object identification defining $\ell_{gf,L}$. On fibre products both maps are induced by the unique canonical isomorphism from the iterated pullback of the final object to $T$, so their equality is independent of the parenthesization. Step 4 transports this equality to $L$. For an identity morphism the same computation uses $1_*J=J$ and gives the identity comparison.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, normalized by the identity resolution; Tag 0D6H, lemma-Leray-unbounded

proof.text:
For an open $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, choose a K-injective resolution $v:j^*J\to H$ using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The derived adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], with the representative characterization in [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general], represents the actual unit at $L=QJ$ by
$$J\xrightarrow{\eta_{j,J}}j_*j^*J\xrightarrow{j_*v}j_*H.$$
Indeed under that characterization this chain map is adjoint to $v:j^*J\to H$, whose class becomes the identity of $j^*L$ after the resolution identification. Both $J$ and $j_*H$ are K-injective by Step 2, so their global-sections map computes $R\Gamma(T,\eta_j)$. By [lem-pur-proetale-open-unit-evaluation], evaluation of the first arrow at $T$ is restriction $\Gamma(T,J)\to\Gamma(U,j^*J)$; evaluation of the second, followed by $\ell_{j,j^*L}$, is $\Gamma(U,v)$. Their composite is exactly restriction followed by its K-injective resolution map, which defines the canonical derived restriction $R\Gamma(T,L)\to R\Gamma(U,j^*L)$. This calculation works for arbitrary open immersions, without quasi-compactness. Step 4 makes it natural in all derived morphisms.

source.place: Tag 0DVC, lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors; Tag 09BN, proetale-lemma-open-immersion, with the unit normalization from lem-pur-proetale-open-unit-evaluation

proof.text: Finally let $B\to C\to D\xrightarrow{d}B[1]$ be the original support-localization triangle. The derived functors in [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] carry it and its pushforward to distinguished triangles. Apply the natural isomorphism $\ell_f$ to its three vertices. Step 4 gives commutative squares for the first two maps and for $d$; Step 5 identifies the fourth-vertex comparison with $\ell_{f,B}[1]$ through the functors' shift maps. Explicitly the last square reads $\ell_{f,B[1]}\,R\Gamma(Y,Rf_*d)=R\Gamma(T,d)\,\ell_{f,D}$ before this shift identification. Thus it is the given third arrow itself, with its given sign and shift comparison, that is identified. If the triangle was rewritten using a composite pushforward, Step 6 gives the same comparisons, and Step 7 identifies its open-unit arrow with restriction.
